topic: Feasible GENE margins and minimax simultaneous orientation of supplied independent cause-effect pairs. Work directly in a positive-density Peters restricted-ANM domain under one explicit fixed regularity envelope and fixed Gaussian kernels. Characterize a local attainable rectangle for the joint population GENE navigation and all-query residual-HSIC margins, and prove the corrected all-procedure frontier N* proportional to log((d+1)/alpha)/lambda there, with a computable simultaneous graph confidence set and matching product-testing converse. Credit Wornbard et al.; novelty must be the F_d geometry and uniform minimax theorem. This is a new attempt at parent eid_gene_population_landscape, not its failed general-landscape classification. Presolve evidence and the exact unresolved uniform-nuisance kill test are embedded in the queue anchor.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the feasible set F_d of joint per-pair GENE correcting-gain and all-query fixed-Gaussian-kernel residual-HSIC margins, and determine whether it contains a nondegenerate local rectangle within one positive-density Peters restricted-ANM regularity envelope.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Peters et al. establish qualitative direction uniqueness, while Li et al. condition their search guarantee on score-landscape behavior. The parent CausalSmith run separately obtained a GENE gain and qualitative reverse-residual dependence but treated the gain and positive HSIC margin as independent promises. Positivity, restricted-ANM non-reversibility, fixed Gaussian bandwidths, and the common regularity envelope couple these coordinates, so their independently specified rectangle need not be realizable. The missing step is a parameter-level Jacobian or direct box-inclusion argument that also remains valid after taking independent products of pairs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local attainability theorem giving an explicit legal ANM parameter chart, an interior base point, and constants for which a displayed product rectangle of navigation and all-query HSIC margins lies inside F_d, with a boundary statement for rank, positivity, or identifiability failure.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent GENE result produces only a sufficient lambda^(-7/3) plug-in rate and explicitly disclaims minimax optimality. Existing HSIC minimax results concern observed variables, whereas ANM orientation uses generated residuals and demands exact recovery of an entire orientation vector. The adjacent score-order proposal supplies only a one-pair pointwise Chernoff calculation for a different margin. A matching lower bound requires opposite-orientation laws that both lie in the attainable F_d chart and have one-sample information distance proportional to lambda; those laws must then be tensorized without letting nuisance estimation or the causal-class restrictions invalidate the product experiment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided theorem with constants c and C showing that a computable procedure has familywise orientation error at most alpha above C log((d+1)/alpha)/lambda and every measurable procedure has nontrivial error below c log((d+1)/alpha)/lambda over the identical F_d class.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent proof controls fitted-versus-oracle HSIC by a first-order Lipschitz telescope in the residual-regression L2 error, which causes the lambda^(-7/3) sufficient order. Gaussian kernels are differentiable, but differentiability alone does not cancel the first-order plug-in term. Raw-variable cross-HSIC theory therefore cannot establish the proposed lambda^(-1) frontier. The unresolved kill test is whether an orthogonalized, degenerate, or bias-corrected expansion makes the generated-residual remainder uniformly smaller than the local testing signal over the same fixed envelope, including all d pairs and every permitted nuisance fit.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit estimator with a finite-sample expansion proving uniform familywise size, power at every HSIC margin lambda once n lambda exceeds C log((d+1)/alpha), and a nuisance remainder below that boundary, or a counterexample showing that no such uniform remainder is possible under the stated envelope.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent confidence-set argument imposes separation on Q_all(B), a query set defined by the realized random bands, without a quantifier making that premise a property of the population law or a controlled event. Replacing it with the full predecessor table repairs determinism but costs exponentially many queries. Supplied independent pairs suggest an O(d) pair-local closure, but it remains necessary to prove path closure for every ternary label realization, measurability of the resulting random set, uniform familywise coverage, and a lower bound preventing honest sets from collapsing prematurely below the product-testing threshold.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit random set C_hat_N contained in {-1,+1}^d with a deterministic O(d) query index, uniform coverage at least 1-alpha, singleton output above C log((d+1)/alpha)/lambda, and a converse forcing non-singleton output with nontrivial probability below the matching threshold.

literature_map:
Li, Qian, Wang, Li, Zhang, and Zhou (ICML 2025) introduce GENE, combining scale-normalized predictive fitness with residual-independence checks.
Their greedy theorem assumes fitness improves as reversal error falls; it does not derive a uniform quantitative margin from ANM primitives.
No web-indexed scholarly record connected “Wornbard et al.” to GENE, ANMs, HSIC, or causal discovery; the verified GENE attribution is Li et al., so the requested Wornbard credit requires queue-anchor verification.
Peters, Mooij, Janzing, and Schölkopf (JMLR 2014; arXiv:1309.6779) prove population DAG identifiability for causally minimal restricted continuous ANMs with positive densities.
That theorem is qualitative and does not bound a GENE navigation advantage or fixed-kernel HSIC separation.
Mooij et al. (JMLR 2016; arXiv:1412.3773) prove consistency of bivariate regression-plus-HSIC orientation under a suitable learner, not a class-uniform finite-sample rate.
Gretton et al. (ALT 2005) define population HSIC and fixed-kernel concentration, without characterizing its attainable values inside restricted ANMs.
Hlávka, Hušková, and Meintanis (JMVA 2011) show that independence tests based on estimated regression residuals need a nuisance-aware expansion.
Kim, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman (Annals of Statistics 2022; arXiv:2003.13208) give nonasymptotic minimax power for permutation U-statistic independence tests.
Berrett, Kontoyiannis, and Samworth (Annals of Statistics 2021) establish matching minimax rates for permutation independence tests.
Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas (JMLR 2023; arXiv:2212.09108) obtain Gaussian cross-HSIC limits and minimax local power for observed-variable independence testing.
These HSIC results do not jointly cover learned ANM residuals, d supplied independent orientation queries, and all-coordinate exact recovery.
Wang, Kolar, and Drton (JASA 2026; arXiv:2305.14506) construct asymptotically valid residual-bootstrap confidence sets for additive-error causal orderings.
Their result does not provide a finite-sample uniform restricted-ANM frontier or an independent-product converse.
Gao and Stoev (Bernoulli 2020; arXiv:1811.05124) distinguish exact simultaneous recovery from average coordinate accuracy, supplying a lower-bound analogy for the logarithmic d factor.
